input.reasoning:
Estimate built bottom-up from the 24 backlog items, mapped to effort by role based on task nature, and scaled by the team's available FTE capacity (Backend 1.5, Frontend 1.0, QA 0.6, DevOps 0.4). Points were used as a relative sizing signal where given (roughly 1 point ≈ 6-7 hours of combined effort for a small full-stack team); unestimated items were sized by analogy to similarly-scoped estimated items and typical complexity (e.g., data migration and design system items are large despite lacking points).

Task-to-role effort split assumptions:
- Backend-heavy: PW-3, PW-4, PW-7, PW-8, PW-9, PW-10, PW-11, PW-14, PW-17, PW-21, PW-22 (auth, integrations, data, infra-adjacent logic)
- Frontend-heavy: PW-2, PW-5, PW-6, PW-13, PW-15, PW-16 (partial), PW-18, PW-19, PW-20
- Shared backend+frontend roughly 60/40 for full-stack features (dashboard, invoices, RBAC UI, tickets)
- QA effort allocated as ~15-20% of dev hours per feature, concentrated on Urgent/High priority items (auth, payments, GDPR, migration) and a dedicated accessibility/regression pass
- DevOps effort concentrated on PW-1 (CI/staging), PW-22 (observability), PW-24 (decommission), plus support hours across payment/migration cutover

Priority weighting: Urgent and High priority items got fuller staffing depth (more QA, tighter DevOps involvement); Low priority items (PW-12, PW-18, PW-19, PW-23, PW-24) were scoped leanly and flagged as first candidates for descope/deferral.

Capacity check: Backend Developer at 1.5 FTE (~2,400 hrs/6-month window) is the primary bottleneck given how backend-heavy the backlog is (payments, RBAC, migration, GDPR, 2FA, rate limiting, notifications, multi-currency, observability). Allocated backend hours are high relative to capacity, so this is flagged as a risk/assumption rather than papered over. DevOps at 0.4 FTE is thin for CI/staging + observability + migration cutover + decommission — flagged as understaffed for the backlog's infra needs. QA at 0.6 FTE is adequate only if QA hours are focused on Urgent/High items and accessibility, not exhaustive coverage of every Low priority item.

No historical actuals exist for this project, so all effort sizing is analogical/expert-judgment based rather than derived from past velocity — this is called out explicitly as an assumption and a source of estimate uncertainty (hence the spread between P50/P80/P95 scenarios).

Non-labour costs include Stripe integration sandbox/fees setup, cloud staging/production infrastructure for the duration, third-party accessibility audit, and a legacy Oracle data migration tooling/consulting contingency line, since 400k+2M record migrations frequently need specialist tooling or DBA consulting beyond the core team's day-to-day rate-carded roles.

scenarios.name: P50 - Base case, full backlog as scoped
P95 - Major rework or scope creep on payments/migration

nonLabourLines.description: Cloud infrastructure (staging + production) for build duration
Stripe integration fees/sandbox and PCI-related tooling
Legacy Oracle data migration specialist consulting/tooling contingency
Contingency buffer (~5% of labour) for unknowns on unestimated tickets

assumptions: No historical actuals/velocity data exist for this project; all effort sizing is expert-judgment/analogy-based, which widens uncertainty in the P80/P95 scenarios.

1 story point ≈ 6-7 combined hours across roles for estimated tickets; unestimated tickets were sized by analogy to comparable estimated tickets (e.g. PW-8 migration sized similarly to a large Urgent item plus a migration-specific premium).

Backend Developer at 1.5 FTE is the primary bottleneck given how backend-heavy this backlog is (payments, RBAC, GDPR, 2FA, multi-currency, rate limiting, migration, observability); allocated hours run close to full capacity for the assumed delivery window, so schedule slippage risk is real if any Urgent item takes longer than planned.

DevOps Engineer at 0.4 FTE is thin relative to the number of infra-touching tickets (CI/staging, observability, migration cutover support, decommission); flagged as understaffed and a likely source of schedule risk or need for temporary contractor support.

QA Engineer at 0.6 FTE hours are concentrated on Urgent/High priority items and a dedicated accessibility pass rather than spread evenly across all 24 tickets; Low priority tickets get minimal QA coverage.
Delivery window assumed to be roughly 6 months for capacity-proportion sense-checking, though no explicit deadline was given.

Legacy data migration (PW-8) assumed to require external specialist/consulting support beyond the core team's rate-carded roles, captured as a non-labour contingency line rather than invented labour hours.
Design system (PW-2) is treated as a foundational Medium-priority item front-loaded early since several UI tickets (dashboard, invoice views, admin back-office) depend on it.
Low priority items (PW-12, PW-18, PW-19, PW-23, PW-24) are scoped leanly and are the first candidates for descope or deferral if budget needs to shrink.

reductions.description: Defer Usage analytics and reporting (PW-19) and Admin back-office (PW-18) to a post-launch phase; both are Low priority and not required for core customer-facing launch.
reductions.effect: Removes ~340 combined backend/frontend hours from initial delivery scope

reductions.description: Descope Contract tests against helpdesk API (PW-23) and Decommission legacy portal (PW-24) from this phase; run them as a fast-follow once the new portal is stable in production.
reductions.effect: Removes ~150 combined backend/DevOps hours; slight risk of undetected helpdesk API drift and delayed legacy shutdown savings

reductions.description: Reduce Multi-currency support (PW-14) to USD+EUR only at launch, adding PLN later once real demand is confirmed.
reductions.effect: Cuts backend FX/settlement complexity by roughly a third

reductions.description: Replace bespoke Support ticket submission sync (PW-12) with a simple outbound webhook/email-to-helpdesk integration instead of full bidirectional sync.
reductions.effect: Reduces backend integration hours while still meeting the core need

reductions.description: Drop the dedicated legacy-migration consulting contingency and instead have the Backend team attempt the Oracle migration in-house with a longer timeline.
reductions.effect: Removes the non-labour contingency line but increases schedule and quality risk given team's lack of migration-specialist experience

reductions.description: Trim Accessibility pass (PW-15) scope to WCAG 2.2 AA on customer-facing screens only, excluding the admin back-office, and skip the external audit in favor of internal review.
reductions.effect: Removes the $6,000 external audit line plus ~40 QA/frontend hours; slightly increases compliance risk for internal tooling
